metadata.purpose: Race-day pacing guidelines for HYROX athletes

pacing_principles.name: Consistent Run Pacing
pacing_principles.rule: Run the exact same physical speed on every single run
pacing_principles.rationale: HYROX is an endurance event. Spiking heart rate early destroys performance on later stations.

pacing_principles.name: Station Management
pacing_principles.rule: Do not go unbroken on heavy stations (Sleds, Wall Balls, Lunges)
pacing_principles.rationale: Breaking early and often keeps heart rate below redline and prevents muscular failure.

pacing_principles.name: The First Run Trap
pacing_principles.rule: Run 10-15 seconds per kilometer slower than your target average pace on Run 1
pacing_principles.rationale: Adrenaline will make you want to sprint. Starting conservative saves glycogen for the back half.

station_specific_tactics.skierg: Smooth, steady pulls. Don't redline here. Use bodyweight, not just arms.
station_specific_tactics.sled_push: Consistent steps. If you stop, keep rests under 5 seconds.
station_specific_tactics.sled_pull: Use your bodyweight to fall back. Manage grip fatigue.
station_specific_tactics.burpee_broad_jump: Find a rhythm. Step up instead of jumping up if heart rate is too high.
station_specific_tactics.rowing: Long, powerful strokes. Similar effort to SkiErg. Don't rush.
station_specific_tactics.farmers_carry: Move quickly but maintain posture. Break before grip fails completely.
station_specific_tactics.sandbag_lunges: Continuous movement if possible. If breaking, rest with bag on shoulders, don't drop it.
station_specific_tactics.wall_balls: Break into manageable sets (e.g., 5 sets of 20, or 10 sets of 10) from the very beginning.
